# Parmana developer docs

> Parmana sets clear limits on what AI agents and business systems may do, checks every action against those limits, and records each decision as a verifiable Execution Trust Record. These pages document the API, the SDKs, the policy model and the operations.

The API is described by an OpenAPI document at https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/site/openapi.bundled.yaml. Experimental Policy version 2 operations are marked as such in that document.

## Get started

- [Parmana developer portal](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/index.html): Parmana makes sure that AI agents and business applications take only the actions the organization has approved, and keeps signed, independently verifiable evidence of each action.
- [Overview](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/overview.html): Parmana is an execution integrity layer for business applications and autonomous AI agents. Before an action runs, Parmana checks that:
- [Getting started](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/getting-started.html): This guide takes you from nothing to a verified execution on your own machine. Every command below was run in the verification for this portal. The steps are in order, and each one ends with something
- [Frequently asked questions](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/faq.html): The first thirteen questions are the ones a developer new to Parmana should be able to answer from this portal alone. The answers are short, and each one links to the page that has the detail and the

- [Policy management](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/policies/index.html): A policy is the organization's rule for one kind of action. Parmana does not decide what your business allows. You write the policy, a second person approves each version, and Parmana enforces it on e
- [Security and cryptographic verification](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/security/index.html): This page explains what Parmana signs, what the signatures cover, how the keys are trusted, and what happens when something goes wrong. The claims are checked against the code and against tests run fo
- [Evidence verification](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/security/evidence-verification.html): This page is for the person who needs to check an Execution Trust Record: an auditor, a second team, a regulator, or your own CI. You can do it without Parmana's server, without the Parmana SDK, and w
- [Schema version 3: whole-record signatures, the cutover and the rollout](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/security/schema-v3.html): This page is the complete reference for schema version 3 (v3). It says what v3 covers, what it does not, how the server and the verifiers are configured, the decision that was made about the downgrade

- [Tutorial: authorize a refund](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/tutorials/refund-authorization.html): payment-refund@1.0.0 has three rules, checked in order. The first matching rule decides:

- [Tutorial: integrate Parmana into a Python application](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/tutorials/python-integration.html): The Python SDK is synchronous only. Call it from a worker, a request handler, or a script. There is no async client.
- [Tutorial: let an AI agent act through Parmana](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/tutorials/ai-agents.html): An agent is a caller with an API key. Its key has a list of capabilities it may invoke, and a list of principals it may act for. Those lists are the only permissions it has. Parmana checks them on eve
- [Tutorial: gate vendor payments in a fintech application](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/tutorials/fintech-integration.html): From fixtures/policies/vendor-payment/2.1.0/policy.json:

- [Endpoint index](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/api/endpoint-index.html): Every operation in openapi/openapi.yaml (94 operations, OpenAPI 3.1.0, API version 1.0.0). "TypeScript SDK method" is the method that sends that exact method and path; "—" means no TypeScript SDK meth

## Operate

- [Deployment and operations](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/deployment/index.html): This page covers running Parmana: local development, Docker, PostgreSQL, cloud, and on-premises. For each option it says whether it is Implemented (in the code, and run here), Implemented, not run her
- [Developer reference](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/reference/index.html): This section is the lookup material: where each definition lives, the complete indexes, the configuration, and the error codes. Use it when you know the name of a thing and want its exact definition.
- [Environment variable reference](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/reference/environment-variables.html): Parmana is configured through environment variables. The server reads them at start-up and refuses to start when a required one is missing or invalid. The SDKs and the CLI read a few more, listed at t
- [Error code catalogue](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/reference/error-codes.html): A Parmana error is an HTTP status plus a body. The body has an error message and, for most refusals, a code. The SDKs turn the status into a class, and keep the server's code where one is sent.
- [Error code index](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/reference/error-code-index.html): 107 error code literals found in the server source. "Triggered in verification" means a request in this portal's runs produced the code. The others are defined in source and were not triggered; their 
- [Troubleshooting](https://pavancharak.github.io/parmana-core/portal/troubleshooting/index.html): This page starts from what you see and works back to the cause. The messages quoted here were observed in this verification, unless a section says otherwise. For the full list of codes, read the error
